\section[be]{\ur{ب} (be) — the letter that opens \ur{بولنا}}

\label{lesson:UR-W34-be}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ur{پ} and \ur{و} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ur{بولنا}} (\emph{bolnā}), \textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ur{ب}}
\textbf{\ur{ب}} — \emph{be}, the sound \emph{b}.

It opens \textbf{\ur{بولنا}} (\emph{bolnā}), \textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{}. You already write \textbf{\ur{پ}}, the shallow boat with three dots beneath it. \textbf{\ur{ب}} is the same boat with \textbf{one dot below}.

\subsection*{Writing: \ur{ب}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/UR-W34-be-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ur{ب} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep the independent be-series bowl from right to left
  \item \textbf{2.} after one lift, place the single dot below — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Be, kāf, and short vowels, independent \ur{ب} handwriting animation and Be instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ur{بولنا}} and point at \ur{ب} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ur{ب} three times, saying \emph{b} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ur{و}, then \ur{ب}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ur{بولنا}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ur{ب}? (\textbf{be}, \emph{b}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ur{بولنا}}, \emph{bolnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[te]{\ur{ت} (te) — the letter that opens \ur{تم}}

\label{lesson:UR-W34-te}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ur{و} and \ur{ب} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ur{تم}} (\emph{tum}), \textquotedblleft{}you (familiar)\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ur{ت}}
\textbf{\ur{ت}} — \emph{te}, the sound \emph{t}, with the tongue against the teeth.

It opens \textbf{\ur{تم}} (\emph{tum}), the familiar \textquotedblleft{}you\textquotedblright{}. The same boat again, now with \textbf{two dots above}.

\subsection*{Writing: \ur{ت}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/UR-W34-te-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ur{ت} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep the independent be-series bowl from right to left
  \item \textbf{2.} after one lift, place the left dot above the main line
  \item \textbf{3.} after another lift, place the right dot beside it — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 2.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Te, mīm, jīm, che, and more diacritics, independent \ur{ت} handwriting animation and Te instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ur{تم}} and point at \ur{ت} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ur{ت} three times, saying \emph{t} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ur{ب}, then \ur{ت}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ur{تم}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ur{ت}? (\textbf{te}, \emph{t}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ur{تم}}, \emph{tum}, \textquotedblleft{}you (familiar)\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ṭe]{\ur{ٹ} (ṭe) — the letter that opens \ur{ٹھیک}}

\label{lesson:UR-W34-tte}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ur{ب} and \ur{ت} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ur{ٹھیک}} (\emph{ṭhīk}), \textquotedblleft{}fine, well\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ur{ٹ}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹ}} — \emph{ṭe}, a \emph{t} made with the tongue curled back.

It opens \textbf{\ur{ٹھیک}} (\emph{ṭhīk}), \textquotedblleft{}fine\textquotedblright{}. Say \emph{tum}, then \emph{ṭhīk}: the first \emph{t} touches the teeth, the second is struck further back. Urdu marks that curled-back sound with a \textbf{small mark above} the boat, where \textbf{\ur{ت}} has its two dots. The dot under the romanization (\emph{ṭ}) marks the same thing.

\subsection*{Writing: \ur{ٹ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/UR-W34-tte-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ur{ٹ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: sweep the independent be-series bowl from right to left
  \item \textbf{2.} after one lift, draw the small retroflex mark downward, back upward, and down again to close its loop — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Zer o Zabar, Fe, qāf, ṭe, ḍāl, and ṛe, independent \ur{ٹ} handwriting animation and Ṭe instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ur{ٹھیک}} and point at \ur{ٹ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ur{ٹ} three times, saying \emph{ṭ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ur{ت}, then \ur{ٹ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ur{ٹھیک}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ur{ٹ}? (\textbf{ṭe}, \emph{ṭ}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ur{ٹھیک}}, \emph{ṭhīk}, \textquotedblleft{}fine, well\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
